# core/ring.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/ring.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Ring buffers and fixed-capacity FIFO queues.

A `Ring` holds only the indices (head, count, capacity); the elements
live wherever the caller keeps them: a `Bytes` for a console or a pipe,
a `Buf` of records for a command queue, a slice of a larger buffer.
`ring_push` and `ring_pop` return the slot to write or read, so one ring
type serves every element type and layout. `Queue` puts a ring and a
`Buf` together for the common case of a FIFO of `u64` words.

What is proved: every slot a function returns is below the capacity,
the count stays between 0 and the capacity, a push claims the slot just
after the last element and a pop the head, and a `Queue` is a FIFO:
`queue_at(q, i)` is its i-th oldest word, `queue_push` appends to that
sequence and `queue_pop` returns its first word and shifts the rest, so
words come out in the order they went in. `queue_at` is opaque: outside
this file a proof sees only those contracts, never the slot arithmetic,
which keeps loops over a queue quick to prove.

`import "core/ring.bastio";`

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Ring`

```bastio
struct Ring {
  h: u64,     // slot of the oldest element
  n: u64,     // number of elements
  cap: u64,   // number of slots
}
```

Head, count and capacity of a ring. Element `i` (0 is the oldest) is
in slot `(h + i) % cap`.

### `Queue`

```bastio
struct Queue {
  r: Ring,
  q: Buf,
}
```

A FIFO of up to `cap` words: a ring over a `Buf` of `cap` words.

## Functions

### `ring_new`

```bastio
fn ring_new(cap: u64) -> Ring
  requires 0 < cap && cap <= 9223372036854775808
  ensures ring_ok(result) && result.h == 0 && result.n == 0 && result.cap == cap
```

An empty ring of `cap` slots.

Example:

```bastio
// A 4-byte console buffer: the ring says where, the bytes live elsewhere.
let mut r = ring_new(4);
let mut buf = balloc(4);
let mut c: u8 = 97;   // 'a'
while !ring_full(r)
  invariant ring_ok(r) && r.cap == 4 && blen(buf) == 4
{
  let s = ring_push(&mut r);
  bset(&mut buf, s, c);
  if c < 200 { c = c + 1; }
}
let first = bget(buf, ring_pop(&mut r));   // the oldest: 'a'
let s = ring_push(&mut r);                 // wraps around to slot 0
let ok = first == 97 && s == 0 && ring_room(r) == 0 && !ring_empty(r);
bfree(buf);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `ring_room`

```bastio
fn ring_room(r: &Ring) -> u64
  requires ring_ok(r)
  ensures result == r.cap - r.n
```

The number of free slots.

### `ring_empty`

```bastio
fn ring_empty(r: &Ring) -> bool
  ensures result == (r.n == 0)
```

Is the ring empty?

### `ring_full`

```bastio
fn ring_full(r: &Ring) -> bool
  ensures result == (r.n == r.cap)
```

Is the ring full?

### `ring_slot`

```bastio
fn ring_slot(r: &Ring, i: u64) -> u64
  requires ring_ok(r) && i < r.cap
  ensures result < r.cap && ring_at(r, i, result)
```

The slot of element `i` (0 is the oldest).

Example:

```bastio
let mut r = ring_new(8);
ring_push_n(&mut r, 6);   // claim six slots at once, as a copy of a run does
ring_pop_n(&mut r, 5);
let at = ring_slot(r, 0);  // the oldest element's slot
assert r.n == 1;
ring_push_n(&mut r, 4);   // runs past the end and wraps
let last = ring_slot(r, 4);
ring_clear(&mut r);
let ok = at == 5 && last == 1 && ring_empty(r);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `ring_push`

```bastio
fn ring_push(r: &mut Ring) -> u64
  requires ring_ok(r) && r.n < r.cap
  ensures ring_ok(r) && result < r.cap && ring_at(old(r), old(r).n, result)
  ensures r.h == old(r).h && r.n == old(r).n + 1 && r.cap == old(r).cap
```

Claims the slot after the last element and returns it: the caller
writes the new element there.

### `ring_pop`

```bastio
fn ring_pop(r: &mut Ring) -> u64
  requires ring_ok(r) && 0 < r.n
  ensures ring_ok(r) && result == old(r).h
  ensures r.n == old(r).n - 1 && r.cap == old(r).cap && ring_at(old(r), 1, r.h)
```

Releases the oldest element and returns its slot: the caller reads it
there (before the slot is pushed again).

### `ring_push_n`

```bastio
fn ring_push_n(r: &mut Ring, k: u64)
  requires ring_ok(r) && k <= r.cap - r.n
  ensures ring_ok(r) && r.h == old(r).h && r.n == old(r).n + k && r.cap == old(r).cap
```

Claims `k` slots after the last element, for a caller that writes
them itself (starting at `ring_slot(r, n)` before the call).

### `ring_pop_n`

```bastio
fn ring_pop_n(r: &mut Ring, k: u64)
  requires ring_ok(r) && k <= r.n
  ensures ring_ok(r) && r.n == old(r).n - k && r.cap == old(r).cap
  ensures k < old(r).cap ==> ring_at(old(r), k, r.h)
```

Releases the `k` oldest elements.

### `ring_clear`

```bastio
fn ring_clear(r: &mut Ring)
  requires ring_ok(r)
  ensures ring_ok(r) && r.n == 0 && r.cap == old(r).cap
```

Empties the ring.

### `queue_new`

```bastio
fn queue_new(cap: u64) -> Queue
  requires 0 < cap && cap <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures queue_ok(result) && result.r.n == 0 && result.r.cap == cap
```

An empty queue of `cap` words.

Example:

```bastio
let mut q = queue_new(3);
queue_push(&mut q, 10);
queue_push(&mut q, 20);
assert queue_at(q, 0) == 10 && queue_at(q, 1) == 20;   // proved FIFO order
let a = queue_pop(&mut q);
queue_push(&mut q, 30);
let b = queue_peek(q);
assert a == 10 && b == 20;
let ok = queue_len(q) == 2;
queue_free(q);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `queue_free`

```bastio
fn queue_free(q: Queue)
```

Frees the queue's storage.

### `queue_len`

```bastio
fn queue_len(q: &Queue) -> u64
  ensures result == q.r.n
```

The number of words in the queue.

### `queue_push`

```bastio
fn queue_push(q: &mut Queue, x: u64)
  requires queue_ok(q) && q.r.n < q.r.cap
  ensures queue_ok(q) && q.r.n == old(q).r.n + 1 && q.r.cap == old(q).r.cap
  ensures queue_from(q, old(q), 0) && queue_at(q, old(q).r.n) == x
```

Appends `x`. A full queue is a precondition, not a run-time error:
callers check `queue_len(q) < q.r.cap` (or drop, as a console does).

### `queue_peek`

```bastio
fn queue_peek(q: &Queue) -> u64
  requires queue_ok(q) && 0 < q.r.n
  ensures result == get(q.q, q.r.h) && result == queue_at(q, 0)
```

The oldest word, without removing it.

### `queue_pop`

```bastio
fn queue_pop(q: &mut Queue) -> u64
  requires queue_ok(q) && 0 < q.r.n
  ensures queue_ok(q) && q.r.n == old(q).r.n - 1 && q.r.cap == old(q).r.cap
  ensures result == get(old(q).q, old(q).r.h)
  ensures result == queue_at(old(q), 0) && queue_from(q, old(q), 1)
```

Removes and returns the oldest word.

## Specification functions

### `ring_ok`

```bastio
spec fn ring_ok(r: &Ring) -> bool {
  0 < r.cap && r.cap <= 9223372036854775808 && r.h < r.cap && r.n <= r.cap
}
```

What every ring function needs and keeps.
(The capacity bound keeps `h + i` from overflowing.)

### `ring_at`

```bastio
spec fn ring_at(r: &Ring, i: u64, s: u64) -> bool {
  (r.h + i < r.cap ==> s == r.h + i) && (r.cap <= r.h + i ==> s == r.h + i - r.cap)
}
```

Slot `(h + i) % cap`, written without `%`: `h + i` is below `2 * cap`.

### `queue_ok`

```bastio
spec fn queue_ok(q: &Queue) -> bool {
  ring_ok(q.r) && len(q.q) == q.r.cap
}
```

### `queue_at`

```bastio
opaque spec fn queue_at(q: &Queue, i: u64) -> u64 {
  get(q.q, (q.r.h + i) % q.r.cap)
}
```

Word `i` of the queue, 0 being the oldest (meaningful for `i < q.r.n`).

### `queue_from`

```bastio
spec fn queue_from(q: &Queue, o: &Queue, k: u64) -> bool {
  forall i: u64 :: i + k < o.r.n ==> queue_at(q, i) == queue_at(o, i + k)
}
```

Word `i` of `q` is word `i + k` of `o`, for every word `o` has from
`k` on.
